mainTopic: Weighing meat and sharpening knives on יום טוב, and whether מכשירי אוכל נפש are permitted
overview: The משנה records a dispute about weighing meat on יום טוב. רבי יהודה allows weighing it against a vessel or cleaver, and חכמים forbid using a scale at all, even just to keep meat away from mice. The גמרא adds more rules: an expert butcher may not weigh meat by hand or in water, a handle-hole in meat may be made only by hand, and an identifying mark may be cut into meat. The גמרא then asks how רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי could weigh portion against portion. It answers that they followed רבי יהושע, and רב יוסף rules like him based on a משנה in בכורות. אביי rejects that proof in two ways, and רב פפא changes who was in the story, since those two sages were not exact with each other. A new משנה forbids sharpening a knife on יום טוב but allows rubbing one knife on another. The גמרא gives four versions of שמואל's comment on when sharpening or cleaning off fat is allowed. רב חסדא explains that the strict view goes against רבי יהודה, who permits מכשירי אוכל נפש, and he himself rules like רבי יהודה. A story about רבא begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה permits weighing meat against a vessel or cleaver
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that on יום טוב a person may weigh meat against a vessel or a cleaver instead of against regular weights.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהודה says: A person may weigh meat against a vessel or against a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with רבי יהודה's view. Meat may be balanced against an ordinary object, such as a vessel or a cleaver, but not against real weights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weighing with real weights looks like a normal weekday business act. Balancing against a vessel or cleaver is an indirect way to measure. The seller can weigh the vessel after יום טוב to find out how much meat he gave, so the price can be settled later.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person may weigh meat
phrases.notes: On יום טוב, when selling or dividing meat.

phrases.english: against the vessel
or against the cleaver.
phrases.notes: The object's weight can be checked after יום טוב.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, meat may be weighed against a vessel or a cleaver, but not against standard weights.

steps.title: חכמים forbid using a scale entirely
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה and say one may not use the pans of a scale at all on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: One may not look at the pans of a scale at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the dispute. חכמים forbid any use of a scale on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים reject רבי יהודה's indirect method. To them, using a scale in any form still looks like weekday weighing. The phrase 'at all' is vague, and the גמרא will explain exactly what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Pay attention to / make use of
The pan of a balance scale

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'look at' literally. Looking at a scale is not forbidden. The phrase means one may not use the scale.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
One may not look at (make use of) the pans of a scale
at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view in the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scale may not be used in any way on יום טוב, not even against a vessel.

steps.title: What does 'at all' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra words 'at all' in the חכמים's ruling come to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the meaning of 'at all'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a clarifying question about the wording of חכמים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding weighing against a vessel already disagrees with רבי יהודה. So the extra phrase 'at all' must add something more. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the meaning of 'at all'?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What additional case the words 'at all' come to forbid.

steps.title: Even to protect meat from mice
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that 'at all' forbids putting meat on a scale even just to keep it away from mice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: Even to protect it from mice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Even a non-weighing use of the scale is forbidden, such as storing meat on a hanging scale so mice cannot reach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is not weighing anything here. He only uses the scale as a safe storage spot. Still, onlookers might think he is weighing, so חכמים forbid even this.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Even to protect it (the meat) from mice.
phrases.notes: Placing meat on the scale only for safekeeping is also forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'At all' includes a non-weighing use of the scale, like guarding meat from mice.

steps.title: Only when the scale hangs ready for weighing
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין limits the ban to a scale hanging on its balancing ring, ready for use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: And this applies only where it is hanging on its ring.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין narrows שמואל's ruling. The mouse-protection ban applies only when the scale is set up for weighing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that people will think he is weighing. That only happens when the scale hangs on the ring used for balancing. If it is not set up for weighing, it is just an ordinary vessel and may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: The ring / hook by which a balance scale hangs for weighing
And this is only when (a limiting formula)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ban is about appearance: a scale is forbidden only when it looks like it is being used for weighing.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
And this is only where it hangs on the ring.
phrases.notes: If it is not hanging ready to weigh, using it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows שמואל's ruling to a specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using a scale to guard meat is forbidden only when the scale hangs on its balancing ring.

steps.title: An expert butcher may not weigh meat by hand
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל forbids an expert butcher from estimating meat's weight by hand on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said that שמואל said: An expert butcher is forbidden to weigh meat by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related rule. An expert butcher may not weigh meat by lifting it in his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An expert can feel the exact weight just by holding the meat. For him, hand-weighing does the same job as a scale, so it is forbidden. An ordinary person's guess is not exact, so this ban is limited to an expert.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
An expert butcher is forbidden
to weigh meat by hand.
phrases.notes: Because he can find its exact weight this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on the same theme of weighing on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expert butcher may not weigh meat by hand on יום טוב.

steps.title: An expert butcher may not weigh meat in water
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל also forbids an expert butcher from measuring meat's weight with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said that שמואל said: An expert butcher is forbidden to weigh meat in water.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, parallel rule from the same speakers. An expert butcher may not measure meat by putting it in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Butchers would put meat in a marked tub of water and see how high the water rose. This gives an exact measure, so it counts as weighing. Like the hand method, it is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: Any method that gives an exact weight, whether a scale, an expert's hand, or water, is forbidden on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
An expert butcher is forbidden
to weigh meat in water.
phrases.notes: By seeing how much the water rises against markings on the container.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling to step 6, applying the same logic to a different method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expert butcher may not measure meat's weight in water on יום טוב.

steps.title: Making a handle-hole in meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי forbids cutting a hole in meat to serve as a carrying handle on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חייא בר אשי said: It is forbidden to make a handle in meat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new related rule. One may not make a hole in a piece of meat to carry it by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a carrying hole into meat is how a butcher does it on a regular weekday. Because it looks like everyday work, it is forbidden on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle (a hole to hold or carry by)

phrases.english: And Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said:
It is forbidden to make a handle in meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from weighing to another butcher-related weekday act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a handle-hole in meat (with a tool) is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: Making the handle by hand is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבינא adds that making the handle by hand is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: But by hand it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא qualifies רב חייא בר אשי's ban. If the hole is made by hand instead of with a knife, it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban targets the normal weekday way of making the hole, with a tool. Doing it by hand is a change from the usual way, so it no longer looks like weekday work.
steps.whatToRemember: Weekday-style acts with meat are forbidden on יום טוב. Doing the act in an unusual way, such as by hand, can make it permitted.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
But by hand it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ban of step 8 to making the handle with a tool.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handle in meat may be made by hand on יום טוב.

steps.title: Making an identifying mark on meat is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא permits marking meat on יום טוב, as רבה בר רב הונא did when he cut his meat into a triangle shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is permitted to make a sign on meat on יום טוב. This is like what רבה בר רב הונא did: he would cut the meat into a three-cornered shape.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds another permitted act with meat on יום טוב. You may cut a mark into it so you can recognize it as yours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps listed things a butcher may NOT do on יום טוב. Here is something that IS allowed. Cutting a simple identifying shape is not treated as a forbidden weekday act. It only keeps your meat from being mixed up with someone else's, for example when a messenger carries it home.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is permitted to make a sign on meat,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: like that of Rabba bar Rav Huna,
who would cut it into three corners (a triangle).
phrases.notes: This marked the meat as his when he sent it home with a messenger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת סִימָן בַּבָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rulings about how meat may be handled on יום טוב. This time the ruling is a leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making an identifying mark on meat on יום טוב is permitted.

steps.title: Two sages weighed portion against portion on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי would divide meat by weighing one portion against another on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון the son of רבי would weigh one portion against another portion on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what two great sages actually did. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They did not weigh the meat against standard weights. They balanced one piece against the other piece so the two shares came out equal. This practice will now be checked against the opinions in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: One portion against another portion, balancing two shares

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi)

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹקְלִין מָנָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: would weigh one portion against another portion on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי שׁוֹקְלִין מָנָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main topic of the משנה, which is weighing meat on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, portion-against-portion weighing was done on יום טוב.

steps.title: Their practice seems to fit neither opinion in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the practice. רבי יהודה allows weighing only against a vessel or cleaver, and the רבנן forbid using a scale at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this follow? It matches neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן! If it follows רבי יהודה, he said that a person may weigh meat against a vessel or against a cleaver. That means against a vessel, yes, but against something else, no. If it follows the רבנן, they said that one may not pay attention to the pans of a scale at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion in the משנה allows what these sages did. It shows that neither side seems to allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows only a vessel or a cleaver as the counterweight. His wording implies that anything else, such as another piece of meat, is not allowed. The רבנן ban any use of a scale on יום טוב. So weighing meat against meat seems forbidden by both views.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion is this?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is the lenient view here, yet his leniency is still too narrow. He permits a vessel or cleaver as the counterweight, which suggests nothing else is allowed.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
Not like Rabbi Yehuda and not like the Rabbis!
If like Rabbi Yehuda, didn't he say:
A person may weigh meat against a vessel
or against a cleaver.
Against a vessel, yes;
against something else, no!
If like the Rabbis, didn't they say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר!
phrases.english: One may not look at the pans of a scale at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? לָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלֹא כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practice described in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי of weighing portion against portion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יהודה, only a vessel or cleaver may serve as the counterweight, so another portion is excluded. Under the רבנן, all use of a scale is forbidden. Either way, the practice has no source.

steps.title: They followed רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that they acted like רבי יהושע. A ברייתא records him permitting portion-against-portion weighing on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They acted like רבי יהושע. As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהושע says that one may weigh one portion against another portion on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. There is a third opinion, רבי יהושע's, and the sages relied on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the only choices were the two views in the משנה. A ברייתא brings a third view that openly permits balancing one portion against another. That fully explains the sages' practice.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: They acted in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.
As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹקְלִין מָנָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: One may weigh one portion against another portion on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a third תנא outside the משנה whose view matches the practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The practice had to fit either רבי יהודה or the רבנן, and it fit neither.
steps.terutzMaskana: The practice follows רבי יהושע, who explicitly permits portion-against-portion weighing.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף decides the הלכה like רבי יהושע, because an anonymous משנה in בכורות agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע, since we learned a משנה in בכורות that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף goes further than explaining the practice. He makes it the practical הלכה, and this sets up the proof brought next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 only showed that the practice had someone to rely on. רב יוסף now declares that this is the final law. His reason is that an unnamed משנה in another מסכת follows the same idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The מסכת dealing with firstborn animals
Like him, in agreement with him

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע: on יום טוב one may weigh one portion of meat against another.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law. Balancing shares against each other is allowed even though regular weighing on a scale is not.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua,
since we learned a mishna in Bekhorot in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 13 into a binding הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע: portion-against-portion weighing is permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: The proof from a blemished בכור
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in בכורות permits weighing portion against portion for a בכור, even though a בכור may not be weighed in the ordinary way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: With disqualified קדשים, the profit from selling them goes to הקדש. And one may weigh one portion against another portion in the case of a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה in בכורות that רב יוסף mentioned. It is the support for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of a blemished בכור may not be sold by regular weight the way ordinary meat is. Yet the משנה still allows weighing portion against portion. This shows that balancing two portions is not treated as real weighing. The same reasoning lets it be permitted on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctified animals disqualified by a blemish
The benefit or profit from them

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from the second half of the משנה, the rule about the בכור. The first half, about profit going to הקדש, is quoted only because it is part of the same line.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Disqualified consecrated animals:
their profit goes to the Temple treasury,
and one may weigh one portion against another portion with a firstborn.
phrases.notes: A בכור may not be sold by regular weight, yet balancing one portion against another is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה that רב יוסף referred to in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The anonymous משנה in בכורות, which permits portion-against-portion weighing for a בכור even though ordinary weighing is forbidden

steps.title: אביי: רבי יהושע may not apply to a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof. He says רבי יהושע may have permitted portion-against-portion weighing only on יום טוב, where no holy item is disrespected. With a בכור, where there is disrespect to holy items, he may forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Perhaps that is not so. רבי יהושע only said his rule here, on a Festival, where holy things are not being disrespected. But there, with a firstborn animal, holy things are being disrespected, so perhaps he would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues that the משנה in בכורות and רבי יהושע might not be saying the same thing, so the משנה cannot prove the הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that רבי יהושע's leniency on יום טוב and the בכורות משנה's leniency for a בכור are one and the same position. אביי says the two cases have different concerns. On יום טוב the concern is weekday activity, while for a בכור the concern is disrespect to holy meat. So רבי יהושע's leniency on יום טוב tells us nothing about a בכור, and the anonymous משנה in בכורות may not match him at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps it is not so (a rejection formula)
He only said his ruling in this case and no further
Disrespect to holy items (here, the meat of a בכור)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי יהושע forbids weighing on יום טוב. He agrees that רבי יהושע permits it there. He is only saying we cannot stretch that ruling to the case of a בכור, so the משנה in בכורות may not be following רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rav Yosef):
But perhaps it is not so,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said his ruling here (on a Festival),
phrases.notes: The 'here' is the case of weighing on יום טוב.

phrases.english: because there is no disrespect to holy things,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָתָם דְּאִיכָּא בִּזְיוֹן קֳדָשִׁים — לָא.
phrases.english: but there (with a firstborn), where holy things are disrespected, he would not permit it.
phrases.notes: Treating a בכור's meat like market meat, weighed for sale, is disrespectful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְדִלְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה in בכורות brought in Steps 14-15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the anonymous משנה in בכורות matches רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes רבי יהושע would permit weighing for a בכור too. But a בכור involves disrespect to holy items, which may make him strict there.

steps.title: אביי's second reason: the רבנן may forbid it on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a second way to reject the proof. The רבנן who argue with רבי יהושע about יום טוב might agree with the משנה in בכורות and permit portion-against-portion weighing for a בכור, because there it does not look like weekday work. On יום טוב it does look like weekday work, so they might forbid it. That means the משנה in בכורות could follow the רבנן instead of רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: the רבנן only said their ruling there, with a בכור, because it does not look like weekday activity. But here, on יום טוב, it does look like weekday activity, so perhaps they would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a second, separate reason why the משנה in בכורות does not prove the הלכה follows רבי יהושע. This time he looks at the issue from the side of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reason, רבי יהושע might be stricter for a בכור. In this second reason, the רבנן might be stricter for יום טוב. On יום טוב, any weighing looks like regular weekday business, which is the main worry. Either way, the two cases are different, so one cannot be used to prove the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Weekday activities, which are improper on יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: אביי gives two reasons why a בכור and יום טוב are different cases. רבי יהושע might be strict for a בכור because of disrespect to holy items. The רבנן might be strict on יום טוב because weighing looks like weekday work. Because of either reason, רב יוסף's proof does not hold.

phrases.english: Alternatively,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said their ruling there (with a firstborn)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מִחֲזֵי כְּעוֹבָדִין דְּחוֹל,
phrases.english: because it does not look like a weekday activity,
phrases.notes: Weighing a בכור is not about regular days versus holy days, so the 'weekday' worry does not apply.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּמִחֲזֵי כְּעוֹבָדִין דְּחוֹל — לָא.
phrases.english: but here (on a Festival), where it looks like a weekday activity, they would not permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent rejection of the same proof that Step 16 rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the anonymous משנה in בכורות matches רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן's leniency for a בכור may depend on the absence of a weekday appearance. That concern is present on יום טוב, so their ruling may not carry over.

steps.title: Were רבי חייא and רבי שמעון really that exact with each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the story of רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי. Weighing their portions suggests they were exact with each other. But in another story, five of the seven fish brought to רבי's house ended up with רבי חייא, and רבי שמעון ברבי did not mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean they were strict with each other? But there were those seven fish that came to רבי's house, and five of them were found in רבי חייא's house, and רבי שמעון son of רבי was not bothered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the original story from Step 11 and challenges it. Why would these two need to weigh meat exactly if they were close like family?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weighing portion against portion only makes sense if each person wants exactly his share. The fish story shows that רבי חייא could take most of the fish from רבי's household with no complaint from רבי שמעון ברבי. So the two did not care about exact amounts, which makes the weighing story hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (introduces a challenging inference)
They were strict or exact with each other
The house of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

phrases.english: Is this to say that they were strict with each other?
But there were those seven fish
that were brought to the house of Rebbi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִשְׁתַּכַּח חֲמֵשׁ מִנַּיְיהוּ בֵּי רַבִּי חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: and five of them were found in the house of Rabbi Chiya,
and Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi did not mind!
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון was רבי's son, so he would have had a claim to the fish. He did not care because they treated each other like family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the halachic discussion and goes back to the facts of the story in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי weighed portion against portion (Step 11).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exact weighing implies the two were careful about getting equal shares. But the fish story shows they did not care about such things with each other.

steps.title: רב פפא: Swap one of the people in the story
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that one name in the story must be replaced with someone else. The pair who weighed the meat was either רבי חייא with רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, or רבי שמעון ברבי with בר קפרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Put another person between them. It was either רבי חייא and רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי, or רבי שמעון son of רבי and בר קפרא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא solves the problem by saying the meat story did not involve both רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי together. One of them was paired with a different scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish story proves only that רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי were not strict with each other. Each of them could still be exact with other colleagues, and those are the pairs רב פפא suggests. Each new pair keeps one of the original names, so the story still works and the weighing makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Put a different person between them (swap one name in the story)
A תנא, the son of רבי יוסי
A scholar of the generation of רבי

steps.whatToRemember: The story of weighing meat on יום טוב is still accepted. Only the pair of people changes: either רבי חייא with רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, or רבי שמעון ברבי with בר קפרא. These pairs were exact with each other about money.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Put another person between them:
phrases.notes: In other words, the original pair was not both of these people. A different person replaces one of them.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: either it was Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי וּבַר קַפָּרָא.
phrases.english: or it was Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi and Bar Kappara.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, שְׁדִי גַּבְרָא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 by changing who was in the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the people in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The weighing was done by רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי together, who were not strict with each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The weighing was done by a pair who were strict with each other: רבי חייא with רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, or רבי שמעון ברבי with בר קפרא.

steps.title: The משנה: No sharpening a knife on יום טוב, but rubbing it on another knife is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids sharpening a knife on יום טוב in the normal way but allows rubbing it on another knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: You may not sharpen a knife on יום טוב. But you may rub it on top of another knife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new topic. It says you may not sharpen a knife on יום טוב, but you may rub one knife against another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sharpening with a real sharpener is normal weekday work, so it is forbidden. Rubbing one knife on another is an unusual way to sharpen, so the משנה allows it. The rest of this passage explains exactly where the line is drawn.

keyTerms.meaning: on top of its fellow (another knife)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may not sharpen the knife on a Festival,
phrases.notes: The normal, weekday way of sharpening.

phrases.english: but one may rub it on top of another knife.
phrases.notes: An unusual way of sharpening, so it is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, separate from the earlier discussion of weighing meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normal sharpening of a knife is forbidden on יום טוב. Rubbing one knife on another is allowed.

steps.title: רב הונא: Only a stone sharpener is forbidden, a wooden one is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה's ban to a stone sharpener. A wooden sharpener is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא said: The משנה only forbade sharpening with a stone sharpener. With a wooden sharpener, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב הונא explains that the משנה's ban covers only a stone sharpener, not a wooden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone sharpener is the normal tool, so using it looks like weekday work. A wooden sharpener is unusual, so it is treated like rubbing knife against knife and is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught (this rule) in the case of

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּמַשְׁחֶזֶת שֶׁל אֶבֶן,
phrases.english: They only taught this regarding a stone sharpener,
but with a wooden sharpener, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּמַשְׁחֶזֶת שֶׁל אֶבֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the משנה's ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies only to a stone sharpener. A wooden sharpener is permitted.

steps.title: First version: שמואל says stone is forbidden only for sharpening, not for cleaning off fat
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל on רב הונא's first half: stone is forbidden only when sharpening, and allowed for scraping off fat. So wood is allowed even for sharpening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What you said, that a stone sharpener is forbidden, applies only when you want to sharpen the knife. But if you only want to scrape off the fat, it is allowed. This shows that with a wooden sharpener, even sharpening is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, adds a condition to רב הונא's stone rule. The forbidden case is sharpening; cleaning the blade is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two questions: which tool (stone or wood) and what purpose (sharpening or cleaning). Here שמואל narrows the stone ban to sharpening only. The גמרא then reasons that wood must be allowed even for sharpening, since שמואל only had to qualify the stone half.

keyTerms.meaning: to remove its fat (to clean the grease off the blade)
we only said this in the case of

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
That which you said, that a stone one is forbidden,
phrases.notes: Responding to רב הונא's first half.

phrases.english: we only said this when one wants to sharpen it,
but to remove its fat, it is permitted.
By implication, with a wooden one,
even to sharpen it is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ שֶׁל אֶבֶן אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the purpose question (sharpening or cleaning) to רב הונא's stone half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stone: forbidden for sharpening, allowed for cleaning. Wood: allowed even for sharpening. This is the most lenient version.

steps.title: Second version: שמואל says wood is allowed only for cleaning, not for sharpening
steps.stepSummary: Others say שמואל commented on רב הונא's second half: wood is allowed only to scrape off fat. So stone is forbidden even for cleaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach שמואל's statement on the second half of רב הונא's words, 'with wood it is permitted.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What you said, that wood is permitted, applies only to scraping off the fat. Sharpening is forbidden. This shows that with a stone sharpener, even scraping off fat is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of שמואל's statement, attached to the wooden half of רב הונא's rule. This version is much stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the allowed case (wood) is narrowed to cleaning only, so sharpening with wood is forbidden. The גמרא then reasons that stone must be forbidden in every case, even for cleaning. Same words of שמואל, but attached to a different place, give the opposite result.

keyTerms.meaning: some teach it (this statement) as referring to
on the latter clause (the second half)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions! Version 1 (step 22): wood allowed even for sharpening, stone allowed for cleaning. Version 2 (here): wood allowed only for cleaning, stone forbidden even for cleaning.

phrases.english: Some teach it as referring to the latter clause:
'With a wooden one it is permitted.'
phrases.notes: Quoting רב הונא's second half.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
That which you said, that with a wooden one it is permitted,
we only said this when one wants to remove its fat,
but to sharpen it, it is forbidden.
By implication, with a stone one,
even to remove its fat is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A rival version of step 22. The same type of comment is attached to רב הונא's second half instead of his first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood: allowed only for cleaning, forbidden for sharpening. Stone: forbidden even for cleaning. This is the stricter of the two versions attached to רב הונא's words.

steps.title: Third version: שמואל comments directly on the משנה, so knife on knife is allowed even for sharpening
steps.stepSummary: Others say שמואל spoke about the משנה itself: the ban on sharpening is only for real sharpening, not for cleaning off fat. So rubbing knife on knife is allowed even to sharpen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach שמואל's statement on the משנה itself, which says: 'You may not sharpen a knife on יום טוב.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This was taught only about sharpening it. But scraping off the fat is allowed. This shows that rubbing it on another knife is allowed even to sharpen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third version. Here שמואל's comment is attached directly to the משנה, not to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, a real sharpener is forbidden only for sharpening and allowed for cleaning. Since the משנה permits knife-on-knife, the גמרא reasons that this must be allowed even when the goal is to sharpen. רב הונא's stone and wood distinction does not appear in this version at all.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three versions of שמואל's comment. (1) On רב הונא's stone half: stone is forbidden only for sharpening, and wood is allowed even for sharpening. (2) On רב הונא's wood half: wood is allowed only for cleaning, and stone is forbidden even for cleaning. (3) On the משנה: a sharpener is forbidden only for sharpening, and knife-on-knife is allowed even for sharpening. In every version, the purpose (sharpening or cleaning) matters.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: the same comment can produce very different practical rules depending on which earlier statement it is attached to.

phrases.english: Some teach it as referring to the Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: 'One may not sharpen the knife on a Festival.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They only taught this when one wants to sharpen it,
but to remove its fat, it is permitted.
By implication, rubbing it on another knife
is permitted even to sharpen it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third rival version. שמואל's comment is moved from רב הונא's words to the משנה itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real sharpener is forbidden only for sharpening and allowed for cleaning. Knife-on-knife is allowed even for sharpening.

steps.title: שמואל's comment placed on the משנה's last clause about knife on knife
steps.stepSummary: A fourth version places שמואל's comment on the משנה's leniency of rubbing knife on knife. It is allowed only to remove fat, not to sharpen. So a sharpener (משחזת) is forbidden even just to remove fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on the last part of the משנה: 'But one may rub it on another knife.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They only taught this when he wants to remove its fat. But to sharpen it is forbidden. This shows that with a sharpener, even removing fat is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives yet another version of where שמואל's comment belongs. This time it sits on the משנה's final clause: knife on knife is allowed only for cleaning, never for sharpening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, שמואל's comment was on the first clause, which made knife-on-knife allowed even for sharpening. Here the same words are placed on the last clause, and they now limit the leniency: knife-on-knife is only for cleaning off fat. The גמרא then reasons that if even knife-on-knife is limited to cleaning, a real sharpener must be forbidden completely, even just for cleaning. This is the strictest version of all.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Rubbing the knife on top of another knife
Its fat or grease, the residue stuck on the knife
A sharpener, a sharpening tool such as a whetstone

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 24. The words of שמואל are the same, but here they are attached to the last clause of the משנה, so they now limit the leniency instead of limiting the ban. That flips the result: knife-on-knife becomes allowed only for cleaning, and the sharpener becomes forbidden entirely.

phrases.english: And some teach it on the last clause:
phrases.notes: Another version of where שמואל's comment belongs

phrases.english: 'But one may rub it on another knife,'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה's leniency

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
They only taught this when it is to remove its fat,
but to sharpen it is forbidden.
This implies that with a sharpener,
even removing its fat is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative version of שמואל's comment, now placed on the משנה's last clause instead of its first
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knife on knife is allowed only to remove fat. A sharpener is forbidden even for removing fat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This strictest version is what sets up the next question: who would forbid a sharpener even just for cleaning?

steps.title: Which תנא forbids using a sharpener?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that using a sharpener is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that a sharpener is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ban on a sharpener follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sharpening a knife does not make food directly. It only gets a tool ready for making food. The גמרא wants to know which תנא forbids this kind of tool preparation on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Which תנא (Sage of the משנה) holds this view?

phrases.english: Who is the Tanna who holds that with a sharpener it is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ban on a sharpener that came out of the previous steps
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא whose view forbids using a sharpener on יום טוב

steps.title: רב חסדא: Not like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the ban on a sharpener does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question: the ban on a sharpener goes against רבי יהודה's view. He brings his source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not name the תנא directly. He identifies the view by contrast: it must belong to the חכמים, who argue with רבי יהודה, because רבי יהודה would allow sharpening.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with, against the view of

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is not like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on a sharpener follows the view that argues with רבי יהודה

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יהודה permits preparing tools for food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is making food (אוכל נפש). רבי יהודה also permits preparing what is needed for making food (מכשירי אוכל נפש).
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation. רבי יהודה permits even the preparations needed for food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב חסדא's answer. It shows that רבי יהודה allows getting tools ready for cooking on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (the חכמים) allows only actual food-making on יום טוב. רבי יהודה adds tool preparation such as sharpening a knife. So the ban on a sharpener must follow the חכמים, not רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Food preparation, the work allowed on יום טוב
Preparations that make food-making possible, like fixing or sharpening tools

steps.confusionAlert: Sharpening a knife is not itself cooking. It is a מכשיר, something that only gets a tool ready. That is exactly the point רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about.
steps.whyThisMatters: The argument over מכשירי אוכל נפש is the key to the whole sharpening discussion. It explains why the rules about sharpening tools on יום טוב are limited.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
There is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat
except food preparation alone.
Rabbi Yehuda permits
even the preparations for food.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that supports רב חסדא's answer
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ban on a sharpener is not like רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה permits מכשירי אוכל נפש on יום טוב and the חכמים do not

steps.title: רבא: We teach in your name that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב חסדא that people teach in his name that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב חסדא: We teach in your name that the הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא checks with רב חסדא whether a ruling taught in his name is correct. This sets up רב חסדא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא just said the ban on a sharpener is not like רבי יהודה. רבא wants to know what רב חסדא himself rules. People were teaching in his name that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, which would allow מכשירי אוכל נפש.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach publicly in your name
The final law follows the view of…

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Chisda:
We teach in your name
that the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא: דָּרְשִׁינַן מִשְּׁמָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from identifying the תנא to asking what the final הלכה is
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב חסדא really rules like רבי יהודה

steps.title: רב חסדא happily agrees: הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says he wishes all such excellent teachings were taught in his name. This means he agrees that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May it be God's will that you teach all excellent teachings like these in my name.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא confirms the ruling. He is happy to have it taught in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'not like רבי יהודה' only identified whose view the ban follows. It was not his own ruling. רב חסדא himself rules like רבי יהודה, so מכשירי אוכל נפש are allowed on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא said the ban on a sharpener is not like רבי יהודה, because רבי יהודה permits מכשירי אוכל נפש on יום טוב. In the end, רב חסדא himself rules like רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: Identifying whose view something follows is not the same as ruling on it. רב חסדא named the opposing view in step 27, but his own ruling follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
May it be God's will
that all excellent teachings like these
you should teach in my name.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהֵא רַעֲוָא דְּכׇל כִּי הָנֵי מִילֵּי מְעַלְּיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא by confirming the ruling
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב חסדא rules like רבי יהודה and is glad it is taught in his name.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: מכשירי אוכל נפש are permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב נחמיה begins a story about רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף begins a story about a time he stood before רבא. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמיה, son of רב יוסף, said: I was standing before רבא, and he was…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story told by רב נחמיה about רבא. This is a setup line, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story will most likely show how רבא acted in practice regarding a knife on יום טוב. A practical example like this tests the rules just discussed. The sentence breaks off here, so the details come on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Nechemya, son of Rav Yosef, said:
I was standing before Rava,
and he was…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story about practical conduct after the ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introductory line of a story. The ruling comes on the next amud.
